scores.rationale: Several snippets from the hypoxia/bioenergetics literature provide indirect support for the idea that lethal DO increases with metabolic activity. Thomas et al. (4, 5) describe how death under hypoxia occurs when maintenance demand exceeds available energy and how increased metabolic demand (ventilation, heartbeat, mobility) raises oxygen requirements, implying that organisms with higher metabolic activity face a death threshold at higher DO. Sokolova (6) frames the lethal range as where required energy flux exceeds aerobic+anaerobic capacity, consistent with higher metabolic demand requiring more oxygen to avoid lethality. HoroCook (2) describes how limiting factors like oxygen constrain active metabolic rate until they become lethal. Weidner (11) notes higher overall metabolic demand requires more oxygen. None contradict the fact. However, no snippet quantitatively and directly demonstrates that lethal DO level rises with measured metabolic rate, so evidence is moderate rather than strong. The remainder of snippets are off-topic (diabetes, exercise, oxidative stress, toxicology). Overall the corpus is consistent with and modestly corroborates the stylized fact.
